title: Kestrel storefront
summary: Customer-facing web shop for refurbished bikes
body: The shop is a Next.js app in the kestrel/web repo, served from Vercel on kestrelbikes.shop. Priya owns it. Product pages are rendered from the shop database and the Typesense index.

title: Checkout flow
body: The cart posts to the payments service and then redirects to the hosted payment page. Apple Pay and iDEAL are enabled. Shipping cost is added before the redirect and orders under 150 EUR pay for delivery.

title: Payments service
body: pay-svc is a Go service that creates Mollie payments and receives the webhook at /hooks/mollie. It writes to the pay_prod database and runs as the Fly app kestrel-pay.

title: Refund policy
body: Customers can return a bike within 30 days. Refunds go back to the original payment method and are triggered from the Mollie dashboard, normally within three working days of the inspection.

title: Inventory sync
body: Every night a job pulls the supplier stock file over SFTP and updates the stock_levels table. If the file is older than 36 hours the job fails loudly instead of zeroing stock.

title: Supplier VeloTrade
body: VeloTrade in Belgium supplies roughly 70 percent of used frames. Contact is Marta. Price lists arrive monthly as CSV and the stock file lives on their SFTP at sftp.velotrade.eu under the account kestrel-sync.

title: Stock alert thresholds
summary: When low stock pings the team
body: A model with three or fewer units in stock triggers a message in the #ops-stock channel. Accessories use a threshold of ten.

title: Recommendation model v2
body: Jonas trains a LightFM model on the events_clean table. Item and user embeddings are exported after each run and the model artifact is uploaded for the serving API to pick up.

title: Feature store
body: Features are defined in Feast. The online store is Redis at redis-feat.internal:6380 and the offline store is the kestrel_ml dataset in BigQuery. Feature definitions live next to the training code.

title: Training schedule
body: Retraining runs on Sundays at 03:00 UTC so fresh weights are ready before Monday traffic. A failed run keeps serving last week's model.

title: GPU box
body: gpu-box-1 is a workstation with an RTX 4090 and 64 GB of RAM running Ubuntu 22.04. It sits in the office rack and is reachable only through the SSH jump host.

title: Jump host
body: jump.kestrelbikes.shop is the only machine with SSH open to the internet. Keys come from the team password manager and fail2ban bans after five bad attempts.

title: Data warehouse
body: BigQuery project kestrel-analytics holds three datasets: raw_events for unprocessed tracking, events_clean for deduplicated sessions, and kestrel_ml for model outputs.

title: Event tracking plan
body: The storefront emits view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase through Rudderstack at /v1/track. Each event carries an anonymous id and, after login, the customer id.

title: Analytics dashboards
body: Metabase runs at bi.kestrelbikes.shop with two collections, Sales and Ops. Questions are written against events_clean and the orders views.

title: Weekly sales review
body: Every Monday at 09:00 the team goes through last week's numbers from the Sales collection: revenue, conversion, return rate and the five best sellers.

title: Customer support tooling
body: Support runs in Zendesk. There are macros for returns, delivery delays and size advice. The target is a first reply within 24 hours on working days.

title: Returns process
summary: What happens to a returned bike
body: Customers write to returns@kestrelbikes.shop, receive a prepaid label, and the bike is inspected in hall 2 when it arrives. Only after inspection does finance release the refund.

title: Sendcloud setup
body: Labels are created through Sendcloud with DHL as the default carrier. The API key lives in Vault under kv/shipping and is read by the shop backend at startup.

title: Warehouse layout
body: Hall 1 holds parts and accessories in aisles A to C. Hall 2 holds complete bikes in aisles D to F plus the photo corner. Fast movers are kept nearest the packing desk.

title: Pick list generator
body: A cron script prints the pick lists at 07:45 so the first shift can start at 08:00. Orders are sorted by aisle to minimise walking.

title: Warehouse printers
body: wh-printer-01 is a Brother QL label printer at 10.20.0.31 loaded with 62 mm rolls. A second spare printer is kept in the cupboard.

title: Ops scripts repo
body: The kestrel/ops-scripts repository contains pick_lists.py, restock_report.py, ebay_sync.py and gdpr_delete.py. They are deployed by pulling main on the cron host.

title: Ops box
body: ops-box.internal is a small Debian 12 VM that runs every cron job. Lena owns it and updates it on the first Tuesday of each month.

title: Restock report
body: On Thursdays the script restock_report.py emails a draft order to buyers@kestrelbikes.shop based on sales velocity and the stock thresholds. Buyers confirm before anything is sent to suppliers.

title: On-call arrangement
body: The on-call phone rotates weekly. Escalation goes to Priya first and then to Jonas. Nobody is expected to respond between midnight and 07:00 unless checkout is down.

title: Incident 2024-03 checkout outage
body: After a deploy on a Wednesday afternoon the checkout returned 502 for about 25 minutes. The new build had a wrong webhook path. We rolled back and added a smoke test for the payment redirect.

title: Deploying pay-svc
body: A merge to main runs the deploy-pay.yml workflow, which builds the image and ships it to Fly. Deploys are avoided on Fridays and during the Monday sales rush.

title: Fly.io apps
body: Two apps run on Fly in Amsterdam: kestrel-pay for payments and kestrel-rec for the recommendation API. Both use a single shared-cpu machine with autoscaling to three.

title: Storefront hosting
body: Every pull request gets a Vercel preview URL. Merging to main promotes to production. Environment variables are set in the Vercel project, never in the repo.

title: Secrets handling
body: Humans use the team password manager. Services read secrets from Vault at startup. Nothing secret goes into environment files that are committed.

title: Vault
body: Vault runs at vault.kestrelbikes.shop with a kv v2 engine. Each service has its own policy that only allows its own path.

title: Domains and DNS
body: The domains were bought at Gandi and DNS is hosted on Cloudflare. kestrel.bike redirects to the main shop domain.

title: TLS certificates
body: Public certificates are managed by Cloudflare. Internal services use certificates from the step-ca instance at ca.internal, renewed automatically every 24 hours.

title: Database backups
body: pg_dump runs every night and writes to the Backblaze bucket kestrel-pg-backups. Backups are kept for 30 days and encrypted before upload.

title: Postgres hosts
body: The main Postgres 16 server is db-main.internal and hosts pay_prod and shop_prod. A read replica db-ro.internal serves reporting queries.

title: Shop database
body: shop_prod stores customers, orders, products and promo codes. Priya owns the schema and every migration needs her review.

title: Restore drill
body: Once a quarter someone restores the latest backup into a scratch database and runs the sanity queries. The last drill took 18 minutes end to end.

title: GDPR requests
body: People ask via privacy@kestrelbikes.shop. The script gdpr_delete.py anonymises the customer and removes marketing consent. We have 30 days to answer.

title: Newsletter
body: The newsletter goes out on Tuesdays through Mailchimp. The main segment is bike-owners and every issue carries the current welcome discount.

title: Promo codes
body: Codes are rows in the promo_codes table. WELCOME10 gives ten percent off a first order. Codes expire automatically at the end date.

title: Admin panel
body: The back office is a Retool app at admin.kestrelbikes.shop. Roles decide who can edit orders, products or promo codes; refunds cannot be issued from it.

title: Pricing rules
body: The shelf price is the supplier price times 1.35, with a minimum margin of 80 EUR. Grade C bikes get a further 15 percent off.

title: Bike grading
body: Grade A is like new, B has light scratches, C has visible wear but is fully functional. The grader notes frame damage and component wear on the intake sheet.

title: Photo workflow
body: Each bike is shot in the photo corner with eight standard angles. Pictures are uploaded to the Cloudinary folder bikes/ and named after the SKU.

title: Cloudinary
body: The Cloudinary account kestrel serves all product images. The transformation preset listing_1600 resizes to 1600 pixels and converts to webp.

title: Product listing template
body: A listing needs the grade, frame size, a short condition note and at least six photos. Sizes follow the manufacturer chart, not the supplier's labels.

title: Marketplace listings
body: A weekly script mirrors selected bikes to eBay and Marktplaats. It skips anything with fewer than six photos and removes sold bikes within a day.

title: Ad budget
body: Maya runs Google Ads at about 1200 EUR per month and Meta at 600 EUR. Spend is reviewed on the first Monday of every month.

title: Brand guidelines
body: The brand colour is Kestrel orange, hex E4572E, on white. Headlines use Inter semibold and body text Inter regular.

title: Design tokens
body: The kestrel/tokens repository exports colours, spacing and type scales as the npm package @kestrel/tokens, consumed by the storefront and the admin panel.

title: TypeScript conventions
body: Strict mode is on. No default exports. The shared lint config @kestrel/eslint-config is mandatory and CI fails on warnings.

title: Python conventions
body: Python 3.11, formatted with ruff. Scripts use uv for dependencies and carry a short module docstring that explains what they do.

title: Git workflow
body: Trunk-based. Small pull requests, one approving review, squash merge. Branch names start with the ticket id.

title: CI pipelines
body: Both kestrel/web and kestrel/pay-svc have a ci.yml that runs lint and tests on every pull request. Required checks block the merge button.

title: Test data
body: Developers seed local databases with seed_dev.sql. Once a week an anonymised dump of shop_prod is produced for staging.

title: Dev environment
body: The kestrel/dev-env repo has a docker compose file: the web app on port 3000, Postgres on 5433 and a Typesense container. Run make up and you are ready.

title: Onboarding
body: Day one is accounts and hardware, day two the dev environment, and by Friday a first small pull request should be merged.

title: Utrecht coworking
body: The team rents desks in a coworking space at Oudegracht 120 in Utrecht. Desks are booked through Deskbird and the wifi password is on the kitchen wall.

title: Holiday policy
body: Full-time staff get 25 days a year plus public holidays. Requests above two weeks need agreement from the team lead.

title: Expense policy
body: Spend through Pleo wherever possible. Receipts are photographed in the app the same day; unreceipted items are not reimbursed.

title: Company cards
body: Every employee can get a Pleo card with a monthly limit of 500 EUR. Limits for buyers are higher and are set by Lena.

title: Accountant
body: Eva at Boekhouder BV does the books and the annual accounts. Sales invoices are issued from Moneybird.

title: VAT handling
body: Sales to other EU countries are declared through the OSS scheme, filed quarterly by the accountant.

title: Moneybird integration
body: A monthly job syncs Mollie payouts into Moneybird. The API token is stored in Vault at kv/finance and rotated yearly.

title: Mollie payouts
body: Mollie pays out daily to the business account and charges about 1.8 percent per card transaction. The payout report is exported for finance every month.

title: Shipping rates
body: DHL parcel delivery within the Netherlands costs 6.95 EUR; orders over 150 EUR ship free. Bulky frames use a pallet service quoted per order.

title: Recommendation API
body: rec-api answers /v1/recs?item= with a p95 of about 40 ms. It loads the newest model artifact at startup and runs as the Fly app kestrel-rec.

title: A/B testing
body: Experiments run on GrowthBook at ab.kestrelbikes.shop. Users are assigned by a hash of their anonymous id so assignment is stable across devices.

title: Experiment log: recommender v2
body: The v2 recommender raised add-to-cart by four percent over two weeks of testing, with no change in return rate. We shipped it to everyone afterwards.

title: Typesense search
body: Typesense at search.internal holds one collection, products. Synonyms such as gravel/cx live in synonyms.json and are loaded on deploy.

title: Search sync
body: sync_search.py reads changed rows from shop_prod every five minutes and upserts them into the products collection. Deleted bikes are removed on the same run.

title: Monitoring
body: Grafana Cloud holds the dashboards and Better Stack watches uptime from three regions. Alerts post to #alerts.

title: Alert rules
body: A checkout error rate above 2 percent for five minutes pages the on-call. Everything else posts to #alerts and waits for office hours.

title: Status page
body: status.kestrelbikes.shop is a Better Stack page. Incidents are posted by whoever is on call within fifteen minutes.

title: Postmortem template
body: Postmortems have four sections: timeline, impact, causes and follow-ups. They are written within three days and discussed in the Monday meeting.
